texts: good. the whenever-condition becomes a fireable rule — any sky-cat hunt on the Cliff Path triggers a lantern-production event tied to that hunt — with the Cliff Path named and typed, "the Hollows" kept as a name, and "many threads" recorded as a vague count on the produced thread group. The lanterns act as one group, so what an individual lantern produces is not separately derivable; that matches what the sentence says, and only needs rewording ("each lantern at the Hollows produces …") if you want per-lantern answers.

good. the lantern group, its location at the Hollows, the produced "thread harvest" with "small" kept as a separate description, and the seasonal time slot are all carried, and the unmarked present correctly reads as a standing seasonal habit rather than one occasion. As in L10-01, "deep winter" lands as one opaque time symbol (deep_winter) that will not link to a plain "winter" elsewhere — a wording-consistency point, not a defect in this sentence.

good. the same shape as the deep-winter sentence and fully covered: lantern group at the Hollows, the produced thread harvest with "steady" as a separate description, and "spring" as a plain season in the time slot.
